newsitem.title: UK: StanChart dragged lower by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: StanChart dragged lower by profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Standard Chartered Plc were among the biggest percentage decliners in the FTSE 100 index by early afternoon on Friday, amid profit-taking at the end of a volatile week for bank shares, dealers said.

Standard reports 1996 earnings next week but traders said profit and dividend growth was expected to be strong and that there were already signs of bargain-hunters coming into the stock at its lower levels.
The stock was down 20p or 2.5 percent at 789 by 1405 GMT in volume of 1.8 million shares.
"Banks were a bit weak in the U.S. yesterday and the (UK) banks have been a volatile sector this week," said one market-maker.

Another pointed to the recent sharp swing in Abbey National Plc shares, down as much as five percent today from yesterday's peak, as an example of volatility in the sector, which has risen sharply in the early weeks of 1997.
Standard is next week expected to post a rise in pre-tax profit to between 860 million stg and 870 million, up from 661 million stg a year before.

First-half profits came in above analyst expectations though chief executive Malcolm Williamson cautioned that the 40 percent growth it had seen in Hong Kong in demand for personal banking services such as mortgages may slow.
